findings.description: The new gate's security premise ("only the owner's comment makes that workflow's review job run, so no outsider can start a recompute-all") holds only because `claude-code-review.yml` lines 36-41 gate its `claude-review` job on `github.actor` and `github.triggering_actor` being the owner, and that file explains the gate only as billing protection. Nothing there says pr-status.yml now relies on it, so loosening the review gate (e.g. letting collaborators run `@claude review`) would silently open the recompute-all to them. A one-line pointer near `claude-code-review.yml` line 31 ("pr-status.yml relies on this owner gate") would make the coupling visible from both sides.

The `if:` comment's trailing "so no outsider can start a recompute-all" repeats the header's "No event an outsider can start does." (lines 7-9); the "only the owner's comment makes that workflow's review job run" half is the real WHY, so the trailing clause can go.
